analysis.title: Global Contenders & Defenders: Momentum reversal, Value bounce
key_insights: Weak-momentum stocks and Value outperformed globally in October while positive-momentum stocks fell. The reversal hurt the Contenders while the valuation component helped.
Global Contenders returned -3.2% in October vs +4.0% for Defenders (a -7.2% gap) and -1.7% for the MSCI AC World. The 12-month performance spread narrowed to 8.4%.
Asia Pac Contenders returned -6.2% in October vs -8.1% for Defenders (+1.9% spread) and beat the MSCI APxJ by 0.7%. The 12-month spread extended to 45.7%.
Three new Global Contenders: Bajaj Auto, Microsoft and NVIDIA. Citigroup is the longest-standing Contender at 25 months. Broadcom, Fortinet and Kia were relegated from the Contenders.
New Global Defenders: Westpac, Xpeng, DNB Bank, Broadcom, IBM, Motorola and Tesla. Relegated from the Defenders: Atlassian, Eternal, F5, MercadoLibre, Bank Central Asia, Skyworks and Handelsbanken.

Five new Asia Pac ex-Japan Contenders: China Citic Bank-H, China Merchants Bank-H, PSBC-H, Tal Education-ADR and Yangzijiang Shipbuilding. Hana Financial is the longest-standing at 18 months. Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, SK Square, Shinhan Financial and Chailease were relegated.
Global Contenders skew to Momentum style (average rank 77) and Defenders to Quality (62). Asia Pac Contenders skew to Value (78) and Asia Pac Defenders are most overweight Risk (46).
Median beta of top-quintile Global Contenders is 1.10, of bottom-quintile Defenders 0.85, of Asia Pac Contenders 0.75 and of Asia Pac Defenders 0.45.

The implied allocation model is most overweight Japan and Taiwan and most underweight the US and India. It is most overweight Banks and Semiconductors and most underweight Consumer Discretionary and Utilities. The biggest recent move was a larger Japan overweight, and a larger Utilities underweight.

Global Contenders returned 19.9% YTD vs 21.0% for Defenders and 9.9% for MSCI AC World. Over 12 months they returned 28.4% vs 20.0% for Defenders. Since May-10 inception they returned 358.1% vs 119.4% for Defenders.

In the Global top-right quadrant (high earnings and price momentum), low-PE stocks underperformed high-PE stocks by 9.8% over 2 years, and the quadrant outperformed the index by 23.4%. Top-right returned -4.8% in October, with high-PE at -7.7% and low-PE at -1.8%.
China-A Contenders returned +1.3% in October vs -4.9% for Defenders and -11.3% for the MSCI China-A Onshore Index.
Micron (MU) has a Contenders Rank of 100 with a market cap of about $999B. Other top-ranked names include Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Petrobras at 100.

risk_factors: Positive-momentum stocks are vulnerable to momentum reversals: high EM + high PM stocks fell 4.8% in October as weak-momentum stocks rallied.
The report says the lists are not recommended and the screen is not a benchmark, so investors should weigh company fundamentals.
Over the last 2 years, low-PE stocks in the top-right quadrant underperformed high-PE stocks by 9.8%, which works against the Contenders' value tilt.

tension_points.bull_case: Contenders combine low PE with strong earnings and price momentum, and outperformed the Defenders by 8.4% over 12 months. The report says Top-Right quadrant stocks outperform in the long term.
tension_points.bear_case: In October the momentum reversal pushed Contenders down 3.2% while Defenders rose 4.0%. Low-PE stocks in the top-right quadrant also lagged high-PE stocks by 9.8% over 2 years.
